reason: Boam AI sells a human-run "fully managed" data service (Toast, Uber Eats, SpotOn) with ~17-23 people across five countries and no technical executive, and its live Ashby posting confesses it is only now hiring "the first product leader at Boam AI" alongside four backend engineering roles - the exact services-to-product, scale-without-headcount transition Daniel Kirichanski sells.

Co-Founder (second founder, commercial/finance side; co-owns the managed-service delivery model)
NOTE: there is no CTO, VP Engineering or Head of Product at this company - that is the signal. Do not search for one; engineering and product both report to the CEO today.
talk_track: I've spent the last few years moving work that lived in people's hands into AI systems that hold up under real load - platform engineering at PayPal and Ripple, then AI agents running incident response at Tricentis. Your Ashby posting for Head of Product says the hire will be "the first product leader at Boam AI" and that "the role starts hands-on: you'll operate as an IC, get your hands dirty, and ship." Open beside it right now: Staff Backend, Senior Backend, Backend, and Security & Backend Engineer. Read together, that isn't a product gap - it's a delivery model where every new enterprise account still costs people, which is why the first product leader has to be an IC. The number that decides how Boam gets valued is cost-to-deliver per account: flat while Toast and Uber Eats volume grows and margin expands; tracking headcount and the next round prices like a service business. Worth knowing either way, even if you never reply. Is cost per account flat or climbing?
